name: Coaching and consulting
result_default: run their first team meetings with confidence

crowd.buyer: People who want one specific result
not_yet: Don't build a course before you've coached 3 people.
Don't pay for ads before you have a story you're allowed to share.
Don't pick a crowd wider than one kind of person and one result.
crowd.note: Needs proof first. January is the busiest month to start.
crowd.basis: research/crowd.json (our judgment); research/niches/coaching.json has no sourced season, so months stay all year.

rules: No earnings, income or results claims in any message, story or offer. Talk about the work you do together, never what someone will earn or achieve.
The free session is free either way. Never ask for a positive story in return.
Share a story only with written permission, after the person approves the exact words.
Wherever a story appears, say the sessions were free, like: Jordan received free coaching sessions.
Leave out health, weight and money results, even true ones.
If something sounds like therapy, medical, legal or investment advice, refer it out.

offer.name: One-to-one coaching
offer.range_text: $75 to $150 a session for newer coaches
offer.basis: From research/niches/coaching.json (Noomii's guide and Thumbtack examples, checked 2026-10-19). ICF's 2023 survey average of $244 to $272 an hour is a ceiling for experienced coaches, not a starting price.
includes: A first session to agree on one result, in your words, and where you're starting
45-minute sessions, every week or every two weeks
A written recap within 24 hours with the actions you chose
steps: A free 20-minute call to see if we're a fit.
Session 1: one result, in your words, and where you're starting.
Every session: check last week's actions, work the next obstacle, choose 1 to 3 actions.
A recap from me within 24 hours.
offer.promise: If I miss a session or I'm late, the next one is free. If the first paid session isn't a fit, I refund it.
offer.promise_note: I don't promise results. You do the work; I bring the structure, the questions and the follow-up. Coaching isn't therapy, medical, legal or financial advice.
sheet_notes: What you share stays private, except where the law requires otherwise.
Move or cancel a session with 24 hours' notice.
If something needs a therapist, doctor, lawyer or financial adviser, I'll say so and help you find one.
offer.footer: Pay per session or per block of 4.

founding.note: For honest feedback at the end. Sharing a story is optional and never part of the price.

intro.note: Your price while you build a track record.

full.note: Raise it when your calendar is 80 percent full.

money_model.name: Block of 4 sessions

keep.title: Reviews, referrals and stories
keep.description: After a block of sessions: a thank-you, an honest review ask with no reward attached, a referral ask, the consent-first story ask and a referral card. No results claims.
keep.done_example: our four sessions on running your team huddle
keep.card_footer: Coaching, not therapy. No results are promised.
rules: Ask every client the same way, not only the happy ones.
Never offer anything for a review. The referral thank-you is for referrals only.
A story is shared only with written consent, with the disclosure line when sessions were free, and never with money or health results.

ai_rules: Never promise results, earnings or health outcomes. Coaching is the work you do together.
Coaching isn't therapy, medical, legal or financial advice. Refer those out.
The next step is the free first session. Say any price once, exactly as given.

stop.label: Asked you to stop
stop.next: Don't send anything else. They're marked lost so they stay off your lists.

yes.label: They're interested
yes.means: They want to hear more or book.
yes.answer: That's great! Let's find a time for the free first session: 45 minutes, and we'll agree on the one result you want. What days work this week or next?
yes.next: Book the free session within 2 days.

price.label: They asked the price
price.means: They want the price before anything else.
price.answer: Of course. Sessions are {rate}, {length} each, with a recap after every one. The first session is free either way, so you can see if it helps before deciding.
price.next: Say the price once, then offer the free first session.

later.label: Not right now
later.answer: No problem at all. Would it help if I checked back in a month or two? The free first session stays open whenever the timing is right.

who.label: Who is this?
who.means: They want to know who you are first.
who.answer: Sorry, I should have said! I'm {me}, and I coach {person} who want to {result}. Happy to answer any question, and the first session is free either way.
who.next: Answer plainly, then offer the free session.

covered.label: They have support
covered.means: They have a coach, mentor or program already.
covered.answer: Good to hear you've got support! If you ever want a second perspective, I'm around. Thanks for letting me know.

question.label: They asked a question
question.answer: Good question! It's easier to answer properly in a quick 20-minute call, free and with no pressure. Would one day this week work?
question.next: Answer it in a line if you can, then offer the call.

other.label: Not sure what they meant
other.answer: Thanks for getting back to me! Happy to help however I can. Would a quick 20-minute call be easier to talk it through?
other.next: Keep it short and end with one question.

talk.label: Wants to talk
talk.means: They want to talk it through first.
talk.answer: Happy to! {when_ask} It's a free 20-minute call, and I'll send you the link before we talk.
talk.next: Book it within 2 days, then run Prep a call before you talk.

objections.label: It's too expensive
objections.means: The price feels high to them.
objections.answer: That's fair. Two smaller ways in: a single session to see if it helps, or the small group at a lower price per person. The first session is free either way.
objections.next: Hold your price. Offer the single session or the group.

objections.label: Can I just do this myself?
objections.means: They wonder if they need a coach at all.
objections.answer: Yes, plenty of people do. What coaching adds is a plan, a weekly check-in and someone to answer to. If you want to see the difference, the first session is free.
objections.next: Agree, then offer the free first session.

objections.label: I don't have time
objections.match: \b(no time|(don'?t|do not) have (the )?time|too busy|so busy|swamped|worried about time|time for (this|it))\b
objections.means: Time is the worry, not the idea.
objections.answer: That's fair, and it's the most common worry. We can meet every week or every other week, and the actions you choose are sized to the week you actually have. Want to try the free first session and see if it fits?
objections.next: Offer the lighter rhythm once, then let them decide.

objections.label: Do you have results?
objections.means: They want to know it works before they commit.
objections.answer: Honest answer: I'm new, so I don't have a stack of stories yet. That's why my first clients get a founding price. Any story I share later is one the client approved in writing.
objections.next: Be honest that you're new. Offer the free first session.

sources.says: Fake or misrepresented testimonials are banned under 16 CFR Part 465, in effect since October 21, 2024.

objections.label: Are you certified?
objections.means: They want to know your background.
objections.answer: Good question. Coaching isn't a licensed profession, so it's fair to ask about someone's background. Happy to walk you through mine on a short call, and I refer out anything that needs a licensed professional.
objections.next: On the call, be specific: your training and experience, nothing more.

objections.label: Is this like therapy?
objections.means: They're checking what coaching is and isn't.
objections.answer: No, coaching isn't therapy. It looks forward at one result you choose. If anything comes up that needs a therapist, I'll say so and help you find one.
objections.next: If they describe a mental health issue, refer them to a professional first.

sources.says: Coaches refer clients with mental health issues to the appropriate professional for diagnosis and treatment.

win.title: Log the new client
win.description: A client said yes: logs the win in your Pipeline, writes the booking message, the prep message and the day-before reminder, and a printable coaching checklist with when to refer out.
win.booking: Hi {greet}, I'm glad we're doing this! Our first session is {when}{where}. It's {deal}.{pay} I'll send the welcome kit with a few questions to answer before we start.
win.prep: Before our first session, have a think about the one result you want, and bring one or two recent examples of where it gets hard. Short answers to the intake questions are plenty.
win.reminder: Hi {greet}, looking forward to our session {when}. Bring one recent example of where it gets hard. Reply here if anything changes.
win.founding: Founding client: at the end, ask {greet} for honest feedback you may quote as a founding client. A story is shared only with their written yes, and it says plainly that they paid a founding price.
win.free: Free sessions: any story from {greet} says plainly that the sessions were free, like this: {greet} received free coaching sessions.

Before session 1: Send the welcome kit: intake questions and the one-page agreement.
Agree the price, how it's paid and the cancellation rule in writing.
Confirm the time and the video link or place.
Every session: Check the actions they chose last time.
End with 1 to 3 actions they choose, with dates.
Send a short recap within 24 hours.
Between and after: One check-in message on the day an action is due.
Every 4 sessions: a progress review against where they started, in their words.
Last session: a written wrap-up, then ask for an honest story with written consent.
If anything points to a mental health, medical, legal or money-advice issue: pause and refer.

sources.says: When a client is experiencing mental health issues, coaches should refer them to the appropriate professional for diagnosis and treatment.
